methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents intentional capacity-building in a secondary city, but its effectiveness will determine whether Roanoke becomes a true secondary hub or remains dependent on NoVA's concentrated expertise for meaningful AI implementation.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-BBB partnership offering AI support to Central Virginia businesses suggests platform-based, shallow adoption spreading beyond metro cores—businesses getting access to AI tools without necessarily building deep internal capability.

signals.title: Pittsylvania County Schools weigh AI policy as technology rapidly changes - Chatham Star-Tribune
signals.signal_reading: Pittsylvania County Schools weighing AI policy signals reactive rather than proactive positioning—rural districts grappling with governance before they have resources or capability, risking falling further behind regions with implementation capacity.

signals.title: Norfolk Public Library to teach people about AI - KCAU 9 News
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Public Library teaching AI literacy represents grassroots, community-level capability distribution through public infrastructure—the kind of broad peer-learning environment that could create distributed fluency beyond elite institutions.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's executive order on AI cyberattacks concentrates security expertise and policy authority at state level, likely benefiting regions with existing cybersecurity clusters (NoVA, Hampton Roads) while other areas lack capacity to implement sophisticated defenses.
